title: CloudBridge POC governance pulse
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on security and compliance progress: SSO integration status, audit log retention and format, data retention policy mapping, SOC 2 artifacts request. SE ran through recent perf/batch tuning changes and implications for logging. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 summary, audit log schema, and updated pilot retention config; CloudBridge to validate SSO cert rotation process and provide test accounts for end-to-end audit trail validation.

Alex Moreno - share SOC2 summary + security whitepaper link by 2027-03-05
Samir Patel - provide SSO test accounts and cert rotation docs by 2027-03-10
Dana Liu - confirm retention windows required for legal/compliance by 2027-03-09

Redwood to push retention/archival config to pilot (30/90/365 day toggles) and notify CloudBridge when done

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes | Attendees: Alex Moreno, Priya Desai, Dana Liu, Samir Patel, Eve Turner

Summary (auto): Quick status on SSO, audit logs and retention; Priya walked through recent tuning changes that affect KV cache and batching; action items agreed.

[00:00] Alex Moreno: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll run about 45 minutes today, mostly security/governance checks then quick perf notes, um Priya do you want to kick off?

[00:18] Priya Desai: yeah thanks Alex, hi Dana, Samir, Eve. Quick on the SSO front — last week we pushed the SAML metadata, we saw CloudBridge IdP accepted, there was one cert chain mismatch which we fixed on our side. Dana, i think you were going to try cert rotation?

[00:36] Dana Liu: yes i rotated the cert yesterday and attempted a login, got a 500 at first then it worked after a cached entry cleared. We did see the audit log entry but the user email was truncated in the message, looked like a transcription thing from our side maybe our proxy shortened it.

[00:52] Priya Desai: hmm okay that's likely the prefix cache on the token service, we saw similar in other pilots where KV cache prefixing cut off long principal names. We'll add a normalization step to the audit exporter so the subject field is full email.

[01:10] Eve Turner: quick question — for retention, legal asked for 7 years for a small subset of transactions, is that something the pilot can do?

[01:24] Alex Moreno: we support configurable retention windows per stream, so we can pin a subset (like auth events) to 7 years in the dedicated or private deployments, hosted has restrictions based on plan and compliance package. For the pilot we'll enable configurable archival and show you export mechanics.

[01:41] Samir Patel: what's the export format for logs? JSON line, Parquet, something else? Our SIEM team prefers parquet for bulk ingest.

[01:51] Priya Desai: currently audit exporter outputs NDJSON by default, plus compressed daily Parquet exports as an option — we can enable the parquet pipeline for you. Note there may be a small cost bump and additional processing latency for on-the-fly parquet conversion.

[02:12] Dana Liu: that's fine as long as the schema matches our fields. Can you send a schema sample? Also we need fields: user_id, principal_email, action, resource_arn, request_id, timestamp, auth_method, and a hashed_payload pointer.

[02:30] Priya Desai: absolutely, i'll export a sanitized sample with field mapping. Side note: some fields currently are named slightly different (we use resource_path not resource_arn) — we'll provide a mapping doc.

[02:46] Alex Moreno: on SOC2 — we got asked to share the SOC 2 type II summary and recent pentest findings, we can share executive snapshot but not raw reports until NDA addendum maybe. We'll send the snapshot.

[03:05] Dana Liu: we can do an addendum, security team prefers to see evidence but we can start with the exec summary.

[03:14] Priya Desai: now shifting to perf changes — last sprint we tuned batching and KV cache eviction to reduce p99 latency for short prompts, this changed some internal logging paths so you might see different request_ids across retries. That can make tracing slightly noisier until we unify tracing ids.

[03:35] Samir Patel: that's a concern for us — our compliance needs to show a single trace across retries for audit. Can you force a consistent trace_id even when retry happens?

[03:46] Priya Desai: yes we can emit a persistent trace_id that's attached at the request ingress and passed through retries, we didn't enable that by default to avoid leaking long-lived ids in public logs but for the pilot we can enable internal-only trace forwarding.

[04:06] Eve Turner: does enabling that change latency or cost?

[04:10] Priya Desai: negligible at token-level, it's mostly a header propagation change. Slightly more metadata per log line, so nominal storage delta.

[04:20] Alex Moreno: another question from legal: do you need log immutability or WORM for archived logs?

[04:28] Dana Liu: we'd prefer WORM for the 7-year set, immutable storage helps for e-discovery.

[04:34] Priya Desai: we can route archival to a WORM bucket on the private deployment or to an S3 bucket with object lock enabled in host mode if you have the right plan. We'll outline options in the doc.

[04:52] Samir Patel: about SSO — our process rotates certs monthly. When you had that cached issue, is there an automated cache invalidation step we need to trigger?

[05:04] Priya Desai: yes we have a cache TTL for metadata and a manual endpoint to invalidate. For the pilot we'll expose a CLI command in the sandbox to request invalidation and we'll document the webhook so you can hook your rotation pipeline.

[05:22] Dana Liu: great — can you also log the cert fingerprint in the audit event so we can reconcile rotations?

[05:28] Priya Desai: yeah adding cert_fingerprint to the auth event is doable. We'll include that in the sample logs.

[05:40] Alex Moreno: quick check — any blockers on SOC2 evidence checklist items? Dana?

[05:46] Dana Liu: i need to see encryption-at-rest proof and KMS integration details (we plan to use our key material). Also need RBAC screenshots from the console and SSO role mapping docs.

[05:58] Priya Desai: we have KMS integrations documented — we support customer-managed keys via HSM/KMS for private deployments; hosted supports bring-your-own-key with rotation and CMK mapping. we'll send screenshots of RBAC console and the role mapping sample.

[06:14] Eve Turner: one compliance wrinkle — our legal team flagged data residency for EU users. We're running a pilot with EU nodes, is the audit log residency tied to the model region or account region?

[06:25] Priya Desai: logs are routed per-route policy; you can pin routing so EU-origin requests get logged to an EU bucket only. We'll show you the per-route policy configuration we used in the pilot.

[06:40] Samir Patel: will that affect latency for EU traffic if logs are stored regionally?

[06:46] Priya Desai: no, logging destination doesn't change model serving path — it's an async export. The only impact is cross-region transfer when you request central aggregation.

[06:59] Alex Moreno: okay let's talk timeline — CloudBridge is trying to close compliance gate by end of month, what's realistic for these items?

[07:08] Dana Liu: end of month is ideal but we can push to two weeks after if needed. We need audit log samples and SOC2 snapshot in the next week to present to legal.

[07:18] Alex Moreno: Redwood will prioritize sending SOC2 summary and sample logs by Friday. Priya will push the parquet export and schema.

[07:27] Priya Desai: i'll also enable trace_id forwarding and add the cert_fingerprint field, then push a retention toggle UI in the sandbox so you can set 30/90/365/9999 (for the 7-year use case) for select streams.

[07:45] Dana Liu: small nit — when you say 9999 days can you map that to explicit years in the doc so legal sees 7 years not a magic number.

[07:53] Priya Desai: yes we'll map numbers to human readable windows.

[08:01] Eve Turner: any updates on costs for the parquet option + long-term WORM storage?

[08:06] Alex Moreno: we'll provide a delta estimate in the pricing doc — expect incremental storage costs and a small processing fee for parquet conversion, and WORM storage priced at market S3 rates with optional retention SLOs if you want long-term cold storage.

[08:22] Samir Patel: one more technical deep item — in our E2E tests we saw a mismatch where the request_id logged by your runtime didn't match the request id surface in the SDK when a fallback to a cheaper model kicked in. That makes audit correlation tricky.

[08:38] Priya Desai: oh yeah that's a byproduct of smart routing fallback — when we reroute to a variant we used to issue a new request_id, we can now propagate the original inbound id and annotate variant_id in the log lines. We'll enable original_request_id on pilot.

[08:56] Dana Liu: perfect.

[09:00] Alex Moreno: any outstanding concerns or unknowns from CloudBridge?

[09:05] Dana Liu: just to confirm the sanitized logs will have no PII, and that the audit export has a consistent timestamp in ISO with timezone.

[09:13] Priya Desai: yes sanitized, consistent ISO8601 timestamps with timezone offsets, we'll standardize on UTC in the samples but keep offset support.

[09:25] Eve Turner: also will you document the playbook for a compliance request — like how to pull historical logs for e-discovery?

[09:32] Alex Moreno: yes we'll include a playbook doc: steps to request archived logs, required approvals, and the format delivered.

[09:40] Dana Liu: about SSO mapping — we need role mapping examples for groups to roles, especially for cross-tenant support.

[09:48] Priya Desai: we'll include example mapping, and a sample SAML assertion mapping doc.

[09:58] Alex Moreno: okay wrapping up. Recap: Redwood to send SOC2 summary, sanitized log samples (NDJSON + Parquet), RBAC screenshots, KMS integration docs; enable trace_id propagation, cert_fingerprint in auth events, parquet export, retention toggles in pilot. CloudBridge to run E2E SSO rotation and share cert rotation docs and retention requirements.

[10:27] Dana Liu: sounds good. I'll look for the docs and run the E2E tests.

[10:34] Samir Patel: i'll set up the SIEM ingest test once we have parquet samples.

[10:38] Eve Turner: i'll coordinate legal/ops review once i have the SOC2 snapshot.

[10:44] Alex Moreno: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with an email and link to the artifacts. Next week same time?

[10:51] Dana Liu: yes, same time works. thanks.

Notes / Links mentioned: Security whitepaper (https://redwood.example.com/security-whitepaper), SOC2 exec summary (link to be shared privately), audit log schema sample (will be uploaded to sandbox), parquet export pipeline doc (internal doc link), pilot retention UI screenshot (attached in follow-up email).

End of transcript.
